bull.b: The sharp revenue and margin rebound shows strong operating leverage and product demand. If elevated NAND pricing and datacenter mix persist, the improved earnings base can support investment and shareholder returns.

Long-term customer commitments improve revenue visibility and deepen strategic ties with datacenter and edge buyers. NBMs exceeding half of bits in FY2027 and roughly two-thirds in FY2028 should reduce reliance on spot-market sales.

bull.t: Strong cash generation and low leverage
bull.b: Cash conversion closely tracking net income and minimal leverage provide substantial financial flexibility. This supports technology investment, supply expansion and capital returns while reducing solvency risk during future NAND downturns.

bear.b: The recent turnaround has not eliminated NAND cyclicality. Prior losses and weak cash generation show that pricing, demand and working-capital swings can rapidly reverse margins, making the durability of current profitability a key risk.

Weakness in PCs and smartphones can pressure volumes and mix in established consumer channels. Although management expects recovery in 2027, prolonged device-market softness could limit diversification while datacenter capacity remains constrained.

Allocation limits may prevent SanDisk from fully converting demand into shipments, while dependence on fewer major NBM customers increases execution and negotiation risk. This can constrain growth and amplify the impact of any program delay.
